materials.text: If they question Brady further about the Eye of Light and Darkness, or tell or show him that they have the half that was left by the pyramid (Nuri of El Wasta, page 320, Egypt), Brady explains that the two halves might make nice bookends, seeing as they cannot be rejoined to form a functioning ward—from his and Mu’s research, once a ward is broken, it’s useless and a new one must be created from scratch. Only the Seven Cryptical Books of Hsan, which he liberated from Lin Yenyu, can help them create new ones (see Deciphering the Seven Cryptical Books, box nearby).

A powerful Elder spell that weakens many Mythos agents and servants. The spell requires a large sacrifice of POW (differing versions vary the amount required). A great sigil of the Eye is worked into a hard, natural substance, such as granite, and then fixed on a high place in the area to be warded. The Eye must be created in the afternoon before the full moon rises. At moonrise, the blood of an innocent (someone without Cthulhu Mythos knowledge) must be used to fill the pupil of the Eye once per hour until the dawn (only a few ounces of blood are actually needed).

The participants must chant as the first blood is given, repeating aloud a phrase that sounds something like, “SA-MA, SA-MA, TE-YO, SA-MA” till the dawn. The ward requires POW from the people chanting (not necessarily given with their knowledge). Each hour of the chant, the Eye leeches 5 POW from each participant until the exact

amount of POW has been absorbed (100 POW for the standard version).

Those losing all of their POW drop dead. If the POW is not accumulated before dawn the activation fails, all leeched energy is lost, and the procedure must be started again from scratch. The Keeper shouldn’t say what is happening until the creation of the ward has succeeded or failed; only then should the players be instructed to mark off the total losses (secretly recorded by the Keeper).

If they question Brady further about the Eye of Light and Darkness, or tell or show him that they have the half that was left by the pyramid (Nuri of El Wasta, page 320, Egypt), Brady explains that the two halves might make nice bookends, seeing as they cannot be rejoined to form a functioning ward—from his and Mu’s research, once a ward is broken, it’s useless and a new one must be created from scratch. Only the Seven Cryptical Books of Hsan, which he liberated from Lin Yenyu, can help them create new ones (see Deciphering the Seven Cryptical Books, box nearby).

Brady and Mu’s research says that the broken Eye of Light and Darkness cannot be repaired into a working ward by joining its two halves. A broken ward is useless: another must be made from the beginning. Brady’s copy of the Seven Cryptical Books of Hsan, taken from Lin Yenyu, provides the means to make new ones.

If the investigators have impressed Brady, either with their knowledge of what’s happening or through their ability to handle themselves, he explains the details of the armed assault he and Firm Action are planning against Gray Dragon Island (The New China Assault Force, page 586) and invites them to join the expedition. If they agree, Brady advises the investigators to find someplace safe to wait; someone will contact them when the moment comes. Time is of the essence and the bad things arranged by Roger’s crazy friends will happen soon if not stopped.

The old Eye of Light and Darkness cannot function again by rejoining its halves: once broken, it is useless and a new ward must be made from scratch. Brady and Mu established this in their research; the Seven Cryptical Books of Hsan taken by Brady from Lin Yenyu provide the means to make new ones. For a new Eye, work a large sigil into hard natural material such as granite and mount it high in the area to be warded. Make it during the afternoon preceding the rise of the full moon. Starting at moonrise, fill its pupil with the blood of someone with no Cthulhu Mythos knowledge, once an hour until dawn; only a few ounces are needed. With the first blood, participants begin chanting aloud until dawn, using a phrase approximately “SA-MA, SA-MA, TE-YO, SA-MA”. The chanting people supply POW, not necessarily knowingly: each hour the Eye drains 5 POW from each participant until the required amount has been collected. The standard version requires 100 POW in total; other versions may differ. Anyone who loses all their POW dies. If the required total is not collected before dawn, activation fails, all drained energy is lost, and the procedure must be restarted from scratch. The Keeper secretly tracks the losses and does not disclose what is happening until success or failure, then tells the players to mark off the totals. This report makes no claim about when a successful Eye becomes active.

Brady and Mu’s research says that the old Eye of Light and Darkness is useless once broken. Joining its halves will not restore a working ward; a new one has to be made from scratch. The Seven Cryptical Books of Hsan taken by Brady from Lin Yenyu can help create new ones. The new ward requires preparation and a ritual with blood, chanting and POW contributions; there are timing restrictions and risks.
